doc.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015

title: Playing versus writing: what he would do more of
summary: Playing is his first love and he misses it more than writing.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: If you could increase one of the things that you do right now — you’re also doing some producing. Would you increase one more thing as opposed to something else?

Well my first love was always playing, so I guess it would be playing. You know it’s hard when I’m writing I usually have to let the playing take a back seat and I don’t practice as much and I occasionally won’t take gigs because if I’m trying to finish a project or whatever. And I kind of miss it. So I miss writing less. If I’m playing a bunch and I’m not writing I don’t miss not writing. I don’t miss writing. But if I’m not playing I really miss it. And it actually affects me psychologically too. I get fidgety, I’m not relaxed, I’m just not as happy a person.
